2-Physical Properties 1-The OH group of phenols allows hydrogen bonding to other phenol molecules and to water. 2-Compared to compounds of similar size and molecular weight, hydrogen bonding in phenol raises its melting point, boiling point, and solubility in water. 8

3- Acidity of Phenols Most characteristic property of phenols is their acidity. Phenols(pKa = 10) are more acidic than alcohols(pKa = 16- 20) but less acidic than Carboxylic acids (pKa = 5). 12
To explain why, let’s compare the ionization of Ethanol and Phenols 13

Substituent Effects on the Acidity of Phenols. 1-Electron-releasing groups ( CH3, OCH3) have little or no effect. 2-Electron-withdrawing groups ( NO2, Cl, OH) increase acidity. 3- Multiple substituent of electron- withdrawing group greatly increase acidity of phenols. 16

5- Reactions of Phenols (C-Ring) A hydroxyl group is very powerful activating substituent, and electrophilic aromatic substitution in phenol occurs far faster, and under milder condition, than in benzene. a- Nitration 31

a- Nitration 32 Phenol reacts with dilute nitric acid at room temperature to give a mixture of 2-nitrophenol and 4-nitrophenol With concentrated nitric acid, more nitro groups substitute around the ring to give 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (old name: picric acid).

33 b- Sulfonation This can be achieved using sulphuric acid at low or high temperature. The low temperature reaction gives ortho substituted product, while at 100oC it gives a para substituted product.

c- Halogenation Bromination of phenol using bromine in carbon disulphide or 1,2-dichloroethane (non-polar solvent) will give o and p bromophenol but with water a polar solvent 2,4,6-tribromophenol is obtained. 34

c- Halogenation  Reaction with bromine water If bromine water is added to a solution of phenol in water, the bromine water is decolourised and a white precipitate is formed which smells of antiseptic. `The precipitate is 2,4,6-tribromophenol. 35

d- Friedel Crafts Reactions  Reaction of alkyl halide with phenol in the presence of Lewis acid gives alkylation, while reaction with alkanoyl chloride gives a ketone. The products obtained are both the o- and p- products. 36
Friedel Crafts Alkylation Friedel Crafts Acylation 37

38 Friedel Crafts Acylation Phenolic esters are often prepared in two steps by means of Fries rearrangement instead of direct acylation. The steps are (i) formation of phenyl esters (ii) migration of acyl group from phenolic oxygen to ortho or para positions.
